```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

necessary libraries. 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringdist)
library(maps)
library(zipcodeR)
```

reading in file. A dataframe is created representing the 1974 spreadsheet
```{r}
grants1974 = read.csv("grants1974.csv", header = TRUE)
```

adding columns based on known info. ID is row number, and we separate source file to create the columns year and month. 
```{r}
grants1974 <- grants1974 %>%
  mutate(ID = row_number(), .before = 1)

grants1974 <- grants1974 %>%
  separate(source_file,
           into = c("year", "month_num", "month"),
           sep = "-") %>%
   mutate(
    month = month.name[match(month, month.abb)]
  ) %>%
  select(ID, year, month, everything(), -month_num)
```

We noticed that many rows are duplicates of previous ones. we remove the duplicates here
```{r}
length(unique(grants1974$grant.number))
grants1974 = grants1974[!duplicated(grants1974$grant.number), ]
```


all columns should be named NEW unless they are blank; will fix it below 
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1974$grant.type))
table(grants1974$grant.type)
```
```{r}
grants1974$grant.type = ifelse(trimws(grants1974$grant.type) == "", "X", "NEW")
```

same thing for program. will rename everything to construction except for the blanks
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1974$program))
sort(table(grants1974$program), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grants1974$program = ifelse(trimws(grants1974$program) == "", "X", "CONSTRUCTION")
```

more complicated errors for step. will look into it below. will use fuzzy matching, a string matching method that assigns a score or distance to an entry on how similar it is to the keywords its analyzing. here, the keywords would be the entries in valid_steps. Based on the distance from each entry to a keyword, we either will or will not assign that entry to the keyword. my algorithm used is below
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1974$step))
sort(table(grants1974$step), decreasing = TRUE)
```
after getting rid of all white space, blank cells turn to X
```{r}
grants1974$step[trimws(grants1974$step) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
valid_steps <- c(
  "STEP ONE",
  "STEP TWO",
  "STEP THREE",
  "STEP TWO AND THREE COMBINED",
  "X"
)

grants1974$step_clean <- valid_steps[
  amatch(grants1974$step, valid_steps, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.20)
]
grants1974$step_clean[is.na(grants1974$step_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$step[is.na(grants1974$step_clean)])
```

```{r}
table(grants1974$step_clean, useNA = "always")
```

my new, cleaned values are in the step_clean column
```{r}
grants1974[, c("step", "step_clean")]
```


Most cells were sorted, but not all; below is an attempt to sort every single cell. ultimately, this does not work out and cells are sorted to values that are incorrect, so we go with step_clean. this workflow is not present in any other file, but i still want to include this here to showcase other methods / options I have tried

```{r}
grants1974$step_match = grants1974$step_clean
bad_rows = which(is.na(grants1974$step_match))

failed_values = grants1974$step[bad_rows]
failed_clean = tolower(failed_values)
failed_clean = trimws(failed_clean)


valid_steps2 = c("step one", "step two", "step three", "step two and three combined")

dist_matrix = stringdistmatrix(failed_values,
                                valid_steps,
                                method = "jw")

repair_match = valid_steps[max.col(-dist_matrix)]
grants1974$step_match[bad_rows] <- repair_match
```

We can find that our attempt to try to label the NA values was not very accurate. Thus, i am going to proceed with the NA values to preserve accuracy. further changes can be made down the line
```{r}
grants1974[bad_rows, c("step", "step_match")]
```
we prefer our cleaning for step_clean, so we override the original column with the clean column
```{r}
grants1974$step = grants1974$step_clean
grants1974 <- grants1974 %>% select(-c(step_clean, step_match))
```

We put Xs in empty columns. other than that we leave this column alone
```{r}
grants1974$title[trimws(grants1974$title) == ""] = "X"
```

For award amount, some cells have $ while others do not. For all cells, i am removing \$ so they can easily be formatted in excel later in time. I also found some had a D instead of an \$. I also adjust this. Some cells are a little more difficult in that some values are not picking up (ex: ,050,000 is a cell but there are numbers before).i mark these values with a Y
```{r}
grants1974$award.amount = trimws(grants1974$award.amount)
flagged_vals = grepl("^[,0]", grants1974$award.amount)
grants1974$award.amount[flagged_vals] = "Y"
grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("\\$", "", grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub(",", "", grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("\\.", "", grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("[A-Za-z]+", "", grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"])
numpart = as.numeric(grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1974$award.amount[grants1974$award.amount != "Y"] = as.character(numpart)
grants1974$award.amount[is.na(grants1974$award.amount)] = "X"
```
a few results to observe that my cleaning was successful
```{r}
sort(tail(table(grants1974$award.amount, useNA = "always")), decreasing = TRUE)
```

award amount should be about 75% of eligible cost. we check this below. If this is not fulfilled then award amount is flagged with checkval, since either award amount or eligible cost can have the error. this also flags if award amount is greater than eligible cost; this shouldn't be possible, so if this is the case, it is also flagged with checkval

```{r}
grants1974$award.amount.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1974$award.amount))
grants1974$eligible.cost.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1974$eligible.cost))

grants1974$award.amount_clean = grants1974$award.amount.num
x_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1974$award.amount.num))
y_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1974$eligible.cost.num))

numeric_rows = !is.na(x_num) & !is.na(y_num)

grants1974$award.amount_clean[
  numeric_rows & (x_num < 0.70 * y_num | x_num > y_num)
] = NA
grants1974$award.amount_clean[is.na(grants1974$award.amount_clean)] = paste0("checkvals_", grants1974$award.amount.num[is.na(grants1974$award.amount_clean)])
```

we observe our results below. my new values are in the award.amount_clean column
```{r}
grants1974[, c("award.amount.num", "award.amount_clean", "eligible.cost.num")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1974$award.amount = grants1974$award.amount_clean
grants1974 = grants1974 %>%  select(-c(award.amount_clean, award.amount.num, eligible.cost.num))
```

For state, we used R's built-in character vector state.abb to match state abbreviations. We also add DC for good measure, PR for puerto rico, VI for virgin islands, and NB, which is what Nebraska was until a later date.
```{r}
sort(table(grants1974$state), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
states <- c(state.abb, "DC", "NB", "PR", "VI")
grants1974$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(as.character(grants1974$state)))

grants1974$state_clean <- grants1974$state_clean |>
  gsub("0", "O", x = _) |>
  gsub("1", "I", x = _) |>
  gsub("5", "S", x = _) |>
  gsub("8", "B", x = _) |>
  gsub("2", "Z", x = _) |>
  gsub("6", "G", x = _)
grants1974$state_clean <- sub(
  ".*\\b([A-Z]{2})\\b.*",
  "\\1",
  grants1974$state_clean
)

grants1974$state_clean <- ifelse(
  grants1974$state_clean %in% states,
  grants1974$state_clean,
  NA
)
sort(table(grants1974$state_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

My new, cleaned column is state_clean
```{r}
grants1974$state_clean[is.na(grants1974$state_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$state[is.na(grants1974$state_clean)])
grants1974[, c("state", "state_clean")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1974$state = grants1974$state_clean
grants1974 = grants1974 %>% select(-c(state_clean))
```

Now we fix award date. i can notice some dates look to be incomplete. thus i am turnign them into NAs
```{r}
grants1974$award.date[trimws(grants1974$award.date) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
clean_date = function(x) {
  
  x = trimws(as.character(x))
  d = as.Date(x, format = "%m-%d-%y")
  return(d)
}
```

We get dates to all have a similar format and represent the correct date. anything that is ambiguous is flagged
```{r}
grants1974$award.date_clean = sapply(grants1974$award.date, clean_date)
grants1974$award.date_clean = as.Date(grants1974$award.date_clean, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1974$award.date_clean = format(grants1974$award.date_clean, "%m-%d-%y")
sort(table(grants1974$award.date_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
grants1974$award.date_clean[is.na(grants1974$award.date_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$award.date[is.na(grants1974$award.date_clean)])
```

for CD, we clean up the cells so that they are all numeric. random nonsense is removed. leading 0s are kept. CDs also only go up to 435, so numbers above that will be flagged
```{r}
clean_num = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  x = gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", x)
  as.numeric(x)
}
```


the old CD column is CD. my new, cleaned column is CD_clean
```{r}
grants1974$CD_clean = sapply(grants1974$CD, clean_num)
grants1974$CD_clean[trimws(grants1974$CD) == ""] = "X"
grants1974$CD_clean[is.na(grants1974$CD_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$CD[is.na(grants1974$CD_clean)])
x_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1974$CD))
grants1974$CD_clean <- as.character(grants1974$CD)
grants1974$CD_clean[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435] <-
  paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$CD[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435])
grants1974[, c("CD", "CD_clean")]
```
We override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1974$CD = grants1974$CD_clean
grants1974 = grants1974 %>%  select(-c(CD_clean))
```

For region, we do something similar to CD. however, we also check if the number of characters is over 2. if it is, then the value is incorrect. usually these values were zipcodes
```{r}
clean_region = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  reg = regmatches(x, regexpr("\\d+", x))
  if (length(reg) == 0 || reg == "") {
    return("X")
  }
  if (nchar(reg) > 2) {
    return("X")
  }
  return(as.numeric(reg))
}
```

```{r}
grants1974$region_clean = sapply(grants1974$region, clean_region)
sort(table(grants1974$region_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grants1974[, c("region", "region_clean")]
```
our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column


Again, we use fuzzy matching to clean census.population. we follow an algorithm similar to the other algorithms we used for fuzzy matching

```{r}
grants1974$census.population[trimws(grants1974$census.population) == ""] = "X"

  "2,500-5,000",
  "X",
  "5,001-25,000",
  "2,500-5,000",
  "25,001-50,000",

  "50,001-125,000",
  "250,001-500,000",
  "125,001-250,000"
)

  amatch(grants1974$census.population, valid_pops, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.25)

table(grants1974$census.population_clean, useNA = "always")
```

for city, we still use the fuzzy matching method. however, we utilize the zipcodesr package to obtain a list of all cities in the US for matching. Thus, the keywords are now the list of cities from the package
```{r}
cities = unique(toupper(zip_code_db$major_city))
grants1974$city[trimws(grants1974$city) == ""] = "X"
valid_cities = c(cities, "X")

grants1974$city_clean <- valid_cities[
  amatch(grants1974$city, valid_cities, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.3)
]

sort(table(grants1974$city_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

We see my new, cleaned entries are below in the column city_clean
```{r}
grants1974$city_clean[is.na(grants1974$city_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1974$city[is.na(grants1974$city_clean)])
grants1974[, c("city", "city_clean")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1974$city = grants1974$city_clean
grants1974 = grants1974 %>%  select(-c(city_clean))
```

From project period, we split the two dates to create two new columns: project.start and project.end. First, we merge project.period and consultant, for we can see that consultant is just a continutation of project.period that gets cut off.
```{r}
grants1974$project.period = ifelse(trimws(grants1974$project.period) == "", grants1974$consultant, grants1974$project.period)
splitdate = strsplit(trimws(grants1974$project.period), split = "THRU")
grants1974$project.start = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 1)
grants1974$project.end = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 2)
```

with these 2 new date columns, we clean them just like we cleaned the previous date columns. No date listed is marked with an ---, whereas an empty cell is given X
```{r}
grants1974$project.start = trimws(grants1974$project.start)
cleaned = gsub("\\s+", "", grants1974$project.start)
grants1974$project.start[grants1974$project.start == ""] = NA
dash_only = grepl("^-+$", cleaned)
parsed = sapply(grants1974$project.start, clean_date)
parsed = as.Date(parsed, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1974$project.start_clean = format(parsed, "%m-%d-%y")
grants1974$project.start_clean[dash_only] = "---"
grants1974$project.start_clean[is.na(grants1974$project.start_clean)] = "X"
```

my new, cleaned entries are below in the project.start_clean column
```{r}
grants1974[, c("project.start", "project.start_clean")]
```
```{r}
grants1974$project.start = grants1974$project.start_clean
grants1974 = grants1974 %>%  select(-c(project.start_clean))
```

```{r}
cleaned = gsub("\\s+", "", grants1974$project.end)
grants1974$project.end[grants1974$project.end == ""] = NA
dash_only = grepl("^-+$", cleaned)
parsed = sapply(grants1974$project.end, clean_date)
parsed = as.Date(parsed, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1974$project.end_clean = format(parsed, "%m-%d-%y")
grants1974$project.end_clean[dash_only] = "---"
grants1974$project.end_clean[is.na(grants1974$project.end_clean)] = "X"
```

```{r}
grants1974[, c("project.end", "project.end_clean")]
```

these edits take place after going through the cleaned excel file and filling in all entries for state. we now validate the entries obtained in the city column. we do this through verifying the city in the original city column is part of the state it is in. if it isn't, it is marked as incorrect. if it is, the city is left the same
```{r}
tempdf = read.csv("1974progress1 - Sheet 1.csv", header = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tempdf$city_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$city))
tempdf$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$state))
tempdf$city_clean[tempdf$city_clean == ""] <- "X"
tempdf$state_validation <- tempdf$state_clean
tempdf$state_validation[
  tempdf$state_validation == "NB"
] <- "NE"

city_state_ref <- unique(
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$major_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    ),
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$post_office_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    )
  )
)

city_state_ref <- city_state_ref[
  !is.na(city_state_ref$city) &
    city_state_ref$city != "",
]



valid_pair <- paste(
  tempdf$city_clean,
  tempdf$state_validation
) %in% paste(
  city_state_ref$city,
  city_state_ref$state
)


tempdf$city_clean[
  !valid_pair &
  tempdf$city_clean != "X"
] <- paste0(
  "incorrect_",
  tempdf$city[
    !valid_pair &
    tempdf$city_clean != "X"
  ]
)

tempdf$state_validation <- NULL
```

```{r}
tempdf[, c("city", "city_clean")]
```

```{r}
tempdf$city = tempdf$city_clean
tempdf = tempdf %>%  select(-c(city_clean))
```

we are now officially done making edits for the spreadsheet in R. as we did a very general cleaning, we still need to go into the spreadsheet and manually fix values. we continue this below after downloading our finished product
```{r}
write.xlsx(tempdf, "1974complete1.xlsx")
getwd()
```
